commands.command: node --test tests/scripts/*.test.mjs   # FIRST time the whole directory is executed
commands.notes: Before any fix: `tests 122, pass 120, fail 2`. Two real failures, both invisible until this run because neither file is invoked by any workflow. This is the measurement that motivated the round.

commands.command: node -e "count test:* scripts and test files not referenced by any .github/workflows/*.yml"
commands.notes: Dormancy census: 12 of the 17 `test:` npm scripts are invoked by no workflow (only test:docs-frontmatter, test:foundation-release, test:release-gate-workflow, test:ci-bench-perf-smoke-workflow and test:generated-marker are wired), and 13 of the 28 files under tests/scripts/ have no npm script at all (branch-hygiene-workflow, check-duplication, check-feature-ledger, check-i18n-generated-scope, check-task-packet-template, harness-check-boundaries, harness-check-encoding, harness-check-generated, harness-check-task-packet-context, harness-graph-review, harness-sort-utils, pr-body-generator plus the new task-manifest-status). A grep for `node --test` or `npm test` in every workflow returns only a path-filter line, so nothing ran them indirectly either.

Failure 1, before the fix: `AssertionError: branch hygiene should run after pushes to main` against a workflow whose `on:` block is only `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`. `git log -p --follow -- .github/workflows/branch-hygiene.yml` shows commit 547427c3 ("chore: simplify workflows for solo developer", PR #142) deleting the `push: branches: - main` trigger, while the test was last touched in bec01d18. The workflow change was deliberate; the test was simply never notified, because it never ran.

Failure 2, before the fix: `a stale baseline entry is reported as a warning` asserted `result.status === 0`, but the 2026-09-23 round tightened check-boundaries.mjs so that `--strict` exits 1 on stale baseline entries (help text: 'Under --strict, a baseline entry that no longer matches any finding (stale) fails'). The test still encoded the old lenient contract. This is a self-inflicted regression from the previous round that no gate could see.

After the fixes: 8/8 pass. The boundaries file now asserts both halves of the documented contract — strict exits 1 on a stale entry, and a non-strict run exits 0 with the stale warning — via a new `runLoose` helper. The branch-hygiene file now asserts the push trigger is absent (with the #142 reference in the comment) and keeps every still-true invariant: no pull_request.closed dependency, pinned actions, contents:write + pull-requests:read, and delegation to scripts/cleanup-github-branches.mjs.

`tests 124, pass 124, fail 0`. Up from 122 tests with 2 failures; the net +2 is the new task-manifest-status file (4 tests) and the new ci-workflow-dispatch wiring guard (1), minus the boundaries stale test that was split into two.

`{ completed: 101, complete: 2, done: 7 }` across 110 manifests, with no manifest missing the field. Three vocabularies for one state, validated by nothing: `status` does not appear anywhere in validateTaskManifest, and no script reads it. A future `status === 'completed'` query would silently miss 9 packets.
`{ completed: 110 }`. The 9 drifting manifests were edited in place (2 `complete` -> `completed`, 7 `done` -> `completed`); no other field was touched and no file was reformatted.

`manifests validated: 110, invalid: 0`, and the probes show the rule is load-bearing rather than decorative: `completed`, `planned`, `in-progress`, `abandoned` accepted; `done` and `complete` rejected with `taskManifest.status must be one of: planned, in-progress, completed, abandoned (got "done")`; `status` absent accepted, so a manifest without the optional field stays legal.

Exit 0. This is the reachability proof for the new rule: check:harness-visual is wired into quality.yml and iterates `listTaskManifestPaths` -> `readTaskManifest` -> `validateTaskManifest`, so every manifest in the repository is validated by a gate that actually runs, not only the ones a task doc links to.
`Task packet check: 28 file(s), 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)`. check:task-packet is wired at quality.yml and reads manifests through readTaskManifest, so it carries the new rule too.

commands.command: node -e "read .github/workflows/ci.yml and assert the test:scripts step exists"
commands.notes: `has test:scripts step: true`. The catch-all runs last in the existing 'Run npm script tests' job, so no new job, runner or cache is introduced.

End-to-end proof the wiring works on the real runner, PR #343 'Unit Tests' job: the log shows `> test:scripts` / `> node --test tests/scripts/*.test.mjs` and then `ℹ tests 124` / `ℹ pass 124`, followed by `✔ ci runs the tests/scripts catch-all so no governance test is left unrun`. The catch-all runs in CI, not just locally, and the guard that keeps it wired is itself executed.

Exit 1 — recorded as a DEFERRED finding, not fixed here: `Evidence check (strict): 93 file(s), 196 error(s)` over legacy artifacts (missing root.repo / root.agent / root.knownGaps / root.linkage in the old commands.json shape). The gate is invoked by no workflow or hook, which is why it has stayed red without blocking anything.

Exit 1 — deferred for the same reason: `Review check (strict): 98 file(s), 51 error(s)`, overwhelmingly `missing ## Machine Readable JSON block` in pre-2026-09 review files. Unwired, so red since it was written.

Exit 1 — deferred: pre-existing subgraph/structural mismatches reported as warnings for the tenant packets (e.g. 2026-09-10-tenant-verification-and-gray: 'manifest vs evidence affected subgraph does not match'). Also unwired (no npm script, no workflow reference). Unrelated to this round's change.

runtimeGap: None. Every claim in this round is a static or local measurement (test counts, manifest census, schema probes, gate exit codes) that was executed on this host; there is no runtime, database, browser or deployment surface involved.

agent.note: Agent: Codebuff (not in the enumerated tool list, so recorded as other). Executed on Windows under Git Bash (Cygwin); `npm` on this host resolves to a broken WSL shim, so every script was invoked as `node <script>` or `node --test <glob>` directly, which is equivalent to the npm script bodies.

knownGaps: check-evidence.mjs and check-review.mjs are listed as expected harness scripts by check-method-health.mjs but are executed by nothing, and are 196-error / 51-error red over the legacy artifacts (93 and 98 files). Wiring them as-is would block every PR, so it needs a legacy allowlist designed the way config/task-packet-legacy-docs.json was — a decision left open rather than taken here.
check-graph-review.mjs is unwired and already reports pre-existing tenant-packet subgraph mismatches; it was not touched in this round.

The new status rule is enforced when a manifest is read, which happens through check:harness-visual and check:task-packet. A manifest that no gate loads is still not validated, so the rule is only as wide as those two paths.

pantheon-ops carries 15 manifests with no `status` and 10 with non-canonical values (`complete` x9, `complete-with-explicit-gates` x1). The inherited schema accepts the missing ones but will reject the drifted ones when ops syncs; normalising them is part of the standing ops deferral and was not done here.

The catch-all runs tests/scripts/*.test.mjs only, so a test placed in a subdirectory (currently only tests/scripts/foundation-release/, which has its own wired script) would still need explicit wiring.
